title: Percentage increase and decrease
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank teaches percentage increase and decrease or reverse percentages; compound interest is a related but different idea taught in Year 12.

draft.title: Percentage increase and decrease
card: To raise an amount by a percentage, multiply by 100% plus the percentage. To increase by 15%, multiply by 1.15.
To lower an amount by a percentage, multiply by 100% minus the percentage. To decrease by 20%, multiply by 0.8.
A $60 jumper is discounted by 20%. New price = 60 × 0.8 = $48.
To find the original amount, divide the new amount by the multiplier. If $48 is the price after a 20% discount, original = 48 ÷ 0.8 = $60. Do not add 20% to $48.
draft.remember: Change forwards by multiplying by the multiplier. Go back to the original by dividing by it.

a.q: A $250 bike is discounted by 30%. What is the new price?
a.why: The multiplier is 100% − 30% = 70%, so 250 × 0.7 = $175. $75 is only the discount, not the new price.

b.q: After a 20% discount, a pair of headphones in Perth costs $120. What was the price before the discount?
b.why: The sale price is 80% of the original, so original = 120 ÷ 0.8 = $150. Adding 20% of $120 gives $144, which is wrong because the 20% was taken from the original price, not from $120.
